generalfeedback.text:
Each kind of argument has its own shape.

  • A direct proof starts from what is known and reaches the conclusion by a chain of logical steps.

  • A proof by exhaustion splits the statement into a finite number of cases that cover everything, and proves each one.

  • A proof by induction proves a first case, then proves that each case leads to the next.

  • A proof by contradiction assumes that the statement is false and shows that this leads to something impossible.

  • A disproof by counterexample gives one example for which the statement is false.

H. S., Roberts, S. and Downey, F., Thinking about Proof, 1st edition, University of Southampton, 2022.
